trigger: a tracked top-level directory whose name starts with `build` is added and holds a session= extractor (none tracked today)
classification_rationale: Unchecked premise of a coverage skip. Defence-in-depth only: check 1 pins the agent log line itself, so a check-2 coverage gap is I8, not I1 (reporter's derivation). Checking the premise needs a git subprocess, an independent surface the #8637 scope did not need (Gate 7 Test 1), so it was split out; later widened by the 8643 issue comment to cover every skipped name.
summary: SKIP_PREFIX="build" silently drops any future tracked top-level build* directory from the #8159 tripwire's scan; the premise (no tracked file under a skipped dir) is unchecked.

trigger: a reader relies on the docstring for the scanned set
classification_rationale: Docstring precision; docs-writer owns wording. Fixed by ee27a738b8.
summary: Module docstring check 2 said 'No text file in the repo', overbroad once SKIP_DIRS and the build* prefix exist.

trigger: a reader of the SKIP_PREFIX comment
classification_rationale: Accurate but incomplete comment. Fixed by ee27a738b8.
summary: SKIP_PREFIX comment did not say top-level FILES named build* are still scanned.

trigger: SKIP_PREFIX widened to "b" or matched case-insensitively
classification_rationale: Regression net (bounded blast radius). Mutation-tested on a scratch copy; fixed by bin/ and Build/ fixtures that must stay flagged. Fixed by ee27a738b8.
summary: Selftest had no negative control for an over-broad prefix: the 'b' and case-insensitive mutants survived.

trigger: large sibling build dirs on a shared runner
classification_rationale: None; cost only. Correct but wasteful; reordered so skipped() runs first. Fixed by ee27a738b8.
summary: iter_files paid is_file()/resolve() per file under build* before skipping it.

trigger: another CI job deletes a directory (skipped build dir or scanned dir) while the gate's rglob walks it, on Python 3.11
classification_rationale: Runner-state false red. Gate 8 r2 unhappy-path verified closure: 40/40 trials ok on 3.11/3.12/3.14 after os.walk + pruning. Fixed by c52b7e5c78.
summary: rglob raised FileNotFoundError on 3.11 when a directory vanished mid-scan (a false red tied to runner state, the #8637 class).

trigger: very large skipped trees (build*, vcpkg_installed, .git)
classification_rationale: Cost against the timeout. Closed by os.walk pruning (150k-file skipped dir: 1.06s -> 0.00s; 1900-deep chain 7.9s -> 0.00s). Fixed by c52b7e5c78.
summary: rglob still descended into skipped trees before filtering, spending time against the 60s meson timeout.

trigger: a directory or file outside the skipped trees is unreadable (mode 000, other-user volume, EIO)
classification_rationale: Silent pass-over of unreadable paths. Recorded with the reporter's facts as stated: I1 derives HIGH, above the reporter's own LOW label, so it is read as BLOCKING until adjudicated (see the superseding row). security-guardian independently derived the same behaviour as I9 (sec8b-1).
summary: The walk passes over a directory it cannot list and a file it cannot read, so an extractor there is never examined and the gate prints OK.

trigger: CI build output under a name outside the build prefix (out/, cmake-build-*, Build-*), or a log copied to the top level
classification_rationale: Residual not covered by name-based skips. Every CI build dir found uses the build prefix; the git ls-files design recorded on the 8643 issue removes this residual by construction.
summary: Residual: build output not under a skipped name can still bring the #8637 false red back.

trigger: TMPDIR inside the checkout plus SIGKILL during selftest_walk; or Defender locking a file at cleanup
classification_rationale: None on CI. Not applicable on CI: TMPDIR is RUNNER_TEMP, outside the workspace (scripts/ci/ci-telemetry.py:104); the yuzu_test_ prefix matches the Defender exclusion; a cleanup error fails loudly, never falsely green (chaos CH-6).
summary: A leftover selftest temp tree inside the checkout would keep later runs red; a cleanup lock would error the test.

trigger: a bare build/ fixture added next to Build/
classification_rationale: Maintenance trap. Comment added at the fixture list. Fixed by c52b7e5c78.
summary: Selftest top-level fixture names must stay distinct after case-folding, or the assertion breaks on NTFS/APFS only.

trigger: a script reachable only through a directory symlink
classification_rationale: None; by design. Deliberate (avoids loops and double scans); now stated in the module docstring.
summary: Directory symlinks are not followed (rglob and os.walk alike), so content reachable only through one is not scanned.

trigger: a flagged file with a non-UTF-8 name
classification_rationale: Degraded diagnostics. Closed by stdout.reconfigure(errors="backslashreplace"); verified under utf-8, cp1252 and ascii. Fixed by c52b7e5c78.
summary: print() of the FAIL line raised UnicodeEncodeError, hiding the remaining FAIL lines (exit still red).

trigger: the gate file itself under a build* directory
classification_rationale: None. Reporter's own analysis: not reachable.
summary: Considered and found unreachable: ROOT is derived from the file's own location and meson runs the source copy.

trigger: a run in which the gate fails is teed to a top-level log (sanitizer-tests.yml tees meson test output to sanitizer-asan.log), then a later run in the same workspace
classification_rationale: The gate's own output trips the gate. Reworded; selftest asserts the emitted message does not self-match; verified end to end (fail, tee, fix, rerun passes). Fixed by c52b7e5c78.
summary: The FAIL message itself contained 'Registered with server' and 'session=', so a captured failure log at the checkout root kept the gate red: the #8637 false red through the still-scanned top-level files.

trigger: a reader relies on the docstring for the scanned set
classification_rationale: Docstring narrower than code. Also raised independently by security-guardian (sec8-1) and docs-writer (doc8-1). Fixed by c52b7e5c78.
summary: Docstring listed fewer exclusions than the code makes (node_modules/.git at any depth, binary files, SELF).

trigger: a reader of commit 3533ae865e's message
classification_rationale: Commit message imprecision. Commit messages are immutable once reviewed; the accurate comparison is recorded here instead.
summary: The commit message calls the build* skip 'the same idiom' as two gates whose skips differ (fixed subtree at any depth; build- prefix only in a git fallback).

trigger: the `p.resolve() == SELF` check is removed
classification_rationale: Regression net. No false-green path: without the SELF check the real run fails loudly on the gate's own fixtures, so CI already pins it.
summary: The selftest walks a temp root, so it never exercises the SELF exclusion; that mutant survives.

trigger: the gate runs on a Big Tam workspace holding the untracked vcpkg clone and gateway/_build* (rebar3)
classification_rationale: Avoidable cost against the timeout on the runners. Recorded with the reporter's facts as stated (I3, E2), which derive above the reporter's own MEDIUM label, so the row reads BLOCKING. Recorder's note, not a de-escalation: a slow CI gate reads as I5/E5 (MEDIUM). Moot for the gate: fixed and re-measured on Big Tam (2.6s at load ~22; 0.4s at load ~32, 7.8k files, no hits). Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: ~110k of ~120k scanned files on a Big Tam workspace were an untracked vcpkg clone and rebar3 output; measured 18-21s at load ~16 against the 60s meson timeout.

trigger: a coverage gcov run leaves *.gcov files at the checkout root and one quotes a session= reader near the Registered line
classification_rationale: Latent false-red vector. The git ls-files design on the 8643 issue removes it by construction.
summary: About 2,500 *.gcov files sit at the root of each Big Tam workspace and are scanned (top-level files are scanned by design); none contain the trigger today.

trigger: residual untracked trees on the Windows and macOS runner pools
classification_rationale: Unmeasured pools. Covered by the same ls-files design on the 8643 issue.
summary: Wee Tam and Big Mags workspaces were not inspected for other large untracked trees.

trigger: the gate's runtime creeps toward the timeout
classification_rationale: Observability nicety. Per-run duration is already recorded by meson and the CI test history; no change.
summary: Suggested printing file count and elapsed time on OK.

trigger: a selftest assertion fails and the traceback is teed to a top-level log
classification_rationale: The gate's own output trips the gate. Same defect and lines as C2-1, raised independently. Recorded with the reporter's facts as stated (I1, E0 derive HIGH); recorder's note: a false red is I8, as C2-1's reporter derived. Moot for the gate: fixed and verified by breaking EXTRACT, MENTION and WINDOW and scanning the captured output. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: A failing selftest's traceback printed assert source/messages containing both patterns, so a captured log could re-trip the gate (C-1 by the stderr route).

trigger: a selftest assertion fails and the traceback is teed to a top-level log
classification_rationale: The gate's own output trips the gate. Assert messages now name the case by index; the fallback literal moved off the assert line. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: Selftest assert messages quoted fixture strings and the fallback literal sat on its assert line, so a failing selftest's output self-matched.

trigger: a scanned directory raises EIO or ENAMETOOLONG on listing
classification_rationale: Silent pass-over of unreadable paths. Recorder's derivation (the reporter gave no impact class), following the adjudicated ruling on the same class (UP-3) and security-guardian's sec8b-1. ENOENT pass-over is the intended UP-1 fix; errno-keyed handling recorded on the 8646 issue.
summary: os.walk(onerror=None) passes over every listing error, where rglob on 3.11 raised on all but permission errors; the UP-3 class, slightly wider.

trigger: a scanned directory chain ~1900 deep on Python 3.11
classification_rationale: None; loud failure. Fails loud, never falsely green; no such depth exists in the tree.
summary: os.walk recursion raises RecursionError on 3.11 (fine on 3.12+); before and after the fix.

trigger: directory symlinks / Windows junctions
classification_rationale: None. No regression.
summary: os.walk does not follow directory symlinks or (3.12+) junctions; same or better than rglob.

trigger: filesystem permissions on the CI checkout make a directory unlistable
classification_rationale: None new. Independent derivation of the UP-3 class.
summary: An unlistable directory or root is passed over silently; unchanged by the fix (UP-3 class).

trigger: the dirnames[:] pruning line is removed
classification_rationale: Regression net. iter_files(root, visited) plus a selftest assertion that no skipped tree is ever listed; the mutant is now killed. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: The selftest did not pin the new pruning (the mutant survived), which carries the UP-1/UP-2 fixes.

trigger: a harness rebinds the module-level ROOT after import
classification_rationale: None. No harmful effect; nothing in the repo rebinds ROOT.
summary: iter_files(root=ROOT) binds its default at definition time.

trigger: a developer reads the FAIL line
classification_rationale: The message names file:line and the fix; the current text is accurate.
summary: Suggested pointing the FAIL message at the module docstring.

trigger: a reader of the docstring exclusion list
classification_rationale: Partly adopted in 7bdc3e66dc (vcpkg named explicitly); the constant is one screen away. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: Suggested spelling out SKIP_DIRS entries in prose.

trigger: the PR merges without its ledger fragment
classification_rationale: CC8.1 evidence. This fragment, committed with the change. Fixed by this ledger fragment.
summary: The governance.d ledger fragment must be committed and cite the 8643 split as an assumed premise.

trigger: the tripwire is read as proof of the #8159 control
classification_rationale: Stated in sec-1's rationale here and in the PR body. Fixed by this ledger fragment and the PR body.
summary: The ledger and PR should say the lexical gate is a regression backstop, not proof of the control (check 1 / the agent code is).

trigger: the PR body overstates the gate
classification_rationale: PR body worded accordingly. Fixed by the PR body.
summary: The PR body should call the gate a best-effort lexical regression tripwire, not an enforcer of #8159.

trigger: a questionnaire cites this gate as evidence for #8159
classification_rationale: None. No customer-facing text cites the gate (checked by enterprise-readiness and compliance-officer).
summary: Do not use the lexical gate as questionnaire evidence for the #8159 claim.

trigger: a future tracked directory named _build* outside gateway/ holds a session= extractor
classification_rationale: Over-broad skip. Anchored to gateway/_build*; selftest asserts _build/, src/_build_helpers/ and gateway/apps/_build_helpers/ stay scanned. Tightening approved by the project owner when asked. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: The `_build*` prune matched at any depth though rebar3 output lives only under gateway/.

trigger: a reader of the pruning comment
classification_rationale: Adopted. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: Comment above SKIP_ANY_DEPTH also explains the vcpkg entry two lines above; suggested 'Also pruned:'.

trigger: a reader of the docstring
classification_rationale: Reflowed and vcpkg named. Fixed by 7bdc3e66dc.
summary: Docstring exclusion sentence was a run-on and hid vcpkg inside SKIP_DIRS.

trigger: visited is appended after pruning instead of before
classification_rationale: None. Equivalent mutant; no action.
summary: Equivalent mutant: visited records the directory listed, not its children, so the order is unobservable.

trigger: the rebar3 prefix match is made case-insensitive
classification_rationale: Regression net. Near-equivalent: rebar3 only emits lowercase _build, and a case-insensitive match would only prune more of gateway/, never source elsewhere (the any-parent and top-level mutants are killed). No action.
summary: That mutant survives: no gateway/_Build* fixture exists.

adjudicated_by: Fraser Jarvis (project owner, not the change author), 2026-11-23, answering the governance runner's adjudication question
adjudication_rationale: Accepted security-guardian's derivation (sec-1, sec8b-1): check 2 is a best-effort coverage backstop and the #8159 control is check 1 pinning the agent log line, so a silently unscanned unreadable path is a coverage gap (I9), not a security-control failure (I1). Pre-existing and unchanged in kind by this PR; whether the gate should fail closed on non-ENOENT errors is a separate decision filed as the 8646 issue. The alternative (fail closed in this PR) was offered and declined.
